design: Resolve the actual setup binary with the shared Cargo/Bazel cargo_bin resolver, preserving the existing Windows resource inspection and asInvoker assertions.

Declare both helper binaries as exec-server Bazel test data and CARGO_BIN_EXE inputs through the existing extra_binaries abstraction. Non-Windows helper main functions are existing panic stubs and these binaries have no Windows-only target-compatibility restriction; the fixture bundle branch compiles only on Windows.

Create a per-fixture Windows directory containing independent copies of the current test executable, setup helper and command runner. The current-exe bundle path travels through the existing ExecServerRuntimePaths and direct-spawn wrapper. Local FileSystemContext and remote ExecServerHarness retain the directory for the operation lifetime.
Independent copies intentionally avoid NTFS hard links because genuine setup may add read ACEs to runtime files; linked copies would share the original build output file security descriptor.

Add only two existing workspace development dependency edges for cargo-bin. No third-party package identity, version, checksum, production lookup, sandbox environment flag, ACL rule, policy assertion or timeout changes.
validation: git diff --check passed for all six paths.
Python TOML parse and package-by-package Cargo.lock comparison confirm exactly two added development dependency edges and no version changes.
Independent source review checked the direct-spawn wrapper, child constructor dispatch and fixture-owned directory lifetime.
No new Rust build, Cargo metadata solve, Bazel analysis, Windows runtime or formatter execution has been claimed in this resource-constrained environment.
required_build_gate: Original just bazel-lock-update plus canonical lock diff review; all original required tests remain active.
limits: The observed eight filesystem integration failures use the direct-spawn wrapper. This repair does not establish coverage of LocalProcess calls that use an in-process native session spawner.

For the focused Cargo sequence, the helper_manifest command builds the Windows-sandbox package binaries before the exec-server command uses them. Merely adding the resolver dependency does not build another package binaries.

The existing remote harness Drop starts asynchronous child termination. Explicit shutdown().await waits for exit, but a destructor-only path can still leave a temporary bundle if Windows holds an image mapping during cleanup; no deterministic cleanup claim is made.
